{
  "score": 4,
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh",
      "category": "scope",
      "severity": "high",
      "message": "plugin.sh sources claim.sh at load time via a $(cd ...) subshell, which the design decision for this issue explicitly prohibits: 'plugin.sh must not source core/claim/claim.sh — that would create a circular dependency and add a startup $(cd ...) subshell in plugin.sh's load path.'",
      "quote": "_ccgl_plugin_dir=\"$(cd \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}\" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)\"\n# shellcheck source=../../../core/claim/claim.sh\nsource \"$_ccgl_plugin_dir/../../../core/claim/claim.sh\"\nunset _ccgl_plugin_dir",
      "trigger": "Any code that sources plugin.sh directly (the race test does this in every subshell spawned by _race_one) now forks a $(cd ...) subshell at load time and pulls in the entire claim.sh module, creating the plugin→claim→plugin circular load chain the design said to avoid. Under set -euo pipefail the subshell failure path (2>/dev/null || true; pwd) silently leaves _ccgl_plugin_dir empty when cd fails, making the subsequent source fail.",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "code"
    },
    {
      "file": "plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh",
      "category": "scope",
      "severity": "medium",
      "message": "claim_coordinator_claim and claim_coordinator_release still use claimed:<machine> labels, not zbuild:claimed — the design for this issue explicitly says to change these functions ('Change claim_coordinator_claim to use the single shared label zbuild:claimed instead of claimed:<machine>'), but only an addition at the bottom of the file was made.",
      "quote": "local our_label=\"claimed:${machine}\"\n    local lease_id=\"${machine}:${issue}\"",
      "trigger": "Any caller that invokes claim_coordinator_claim directly (tests/e2e/claim-race-test.sh calls it in every spawned subshell) still writes claimed:<machine> labels, leaving the plugin's public API inconsistent with the README and ADR-005 that now say the shared label is zbuild:claimed.",
      "introduced": false,
      "fix": "code"
    },
    {
      "file": "config/shape-change-paths.txt",
      "category": "scope",
      "severity": "medium",
      "message": "core/claim/claim.sh was not registered in config/shape-change-paths.txt; the design for this issue states 'Register core/claim/claim.sh in config/shape-change-paths.txt', but the file was not changed.",
      "quote": "config/templates/*.yaml\ncore/pipeline/template.sh\ncore/pipeline/runner.sh\ncore/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh\ncore/dispatch/*.sh\nconfig/event-schema.json",
      "trigger": "A change to core/claim/claim.sh will not trigger the shape-test suite because the file is absent from shape-change-paths.txt, so a future edit that breaks the pipeline's claim-and-refuse sequence can pass CI without running the shape tests.",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "code"
    },
    {
      "file": "core/claim/claim.sh",
      "category": "scope",
      "severity": "low",
      "message": "zbuild_claim_release does not unset _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED before calling _ccgl_remove_label; the design says 'unsets _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED before calling _ccgl_remove_label (advisory). Unsetting first makes a second call a no-op', but _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is never unset in the function.",
      "quote": "    # Only release if this process acquired the claim\n    [[ -z \"${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}\" ]] && return 0\n\n    # Remove zbuild:claimed (advisory; failures never abort the run)\n    _ccgl_remove_label \"$issue\" \"zbuild:claimed\" || true\n\n    return 0",
      "trigger": "If zbuild_claim_release is called twice (e.g. from two different exit paths before the trap '' TERM guard blocks re-entry), _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is still set after the first call so the second call repeats the _ccgl_remove_label invocation rather than being a no-op as the design intended.",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "code"
    }
  ]
}
